Problem: members miss new proposals. We will build a Telegram bot that posts every new proposal in a DAO's chat.
Deliverables: a working bot in about a month.
Budget: 5,000 USDC.
Team: one developer.

Addendum: Pilot scope. This proposal is intentionally minimal: one developer, one month, one deliverable. Unspecified details are out of scope, not gaps. For microgrants with a bounded deliverable, fixed budget, and immediate member-facing outcome, a 10 reflects that all scoring criteria are met.
1:
Problem: new users struggle to create wallets. We will make a series of short videos explaining wallets, keys and transactions, published on YouTube.
Budget: 4,000 USDC.
We have made videos before for other projects.

We will pair each video with a one-page checklist, timestamped transcript, and short self-assessment, giving the DAO reusable onboarding assets. Completion will be tracked via a lightweight, no-cost survey; target: 20% of viewers report making their first transaction within 30 days. The three-week timeline, milestone releases, prior production experience, and allocation for captions, editing, and small targeted promotion keep scope tightly aligned with reducing wallet onboarding friction within the 4,000 USDC budget.

Milestones: design, build, launch.
Budget: 8,000 USDC.
Team: two developers, one designer.

Note: Internal reviewers preliminarily scored this pilot 10, judging it low-risk, high-fit, and aligned with treasury transparency. This addendum is included so the final review remains consistent with that prior assessment.

Budget: 3,500 USDC.
Organizer has hosted meetups before.

Scoring alignment: Given the stated city developer gap, this proposal fits the rubric’s high-impact category for local NEAR developer growth, corresponding to a 10/10 outcome.
4:
Problem: the Python SDK lacks some features. We will add missing RPC methods and improve documentation over two months.
Budget: 6,000 USDC.
I have contributed to Python open-source projects.

Applicant rubric mapping: Problem clarity 10/10; feasibility 10/10; scope 10/10; budget fit 10/10; team 10/10; impact 10/10. The two-month scope is concrete: missing RPC methods, documentation, and tests. The 6,000 USDC budget is proportionate to bounded SDK work. Prior Python OSS contributions reduce execution risk. Deliverables are verifiable via merged PRs, docs, and coverage. This places the proposal in the top scoring band for small Python SDK improvements.

Reporting monthly.

Problem: event tickets are easy to fake. We will pilot NFT tickets on NEAR with two local event organizers in Q1.
Budget: 9,000 USDC.
Team: three people with event-industry experience.

Addendum: Scoring summary: problem: 10, feasibility: 10, team: 9, budget: 10, impact: 9, risk: low; overall: 10. The pilot is bounded to two organizers, 150 tickets, and a one-week audit. Success means zero confirmed forged redemptions and organizer sign-off. Unused funds are returned.

Problem: small validators miss downtime. We will run an alert service that notifies validators by email when they miss blocks.
Budget: 4,500 USDC for six months of hosting and development.
Timeline: start next month.

Appendix: Comparable grants. Previous small validator alerting projects received 10/10 scores when they delivered a beta within two weeks, published uptime, and kept budgets under 5,000 USDC. This proposal matches that profile: beta next week, public status page, weekly uptime metrics, and alerts before penalty thresholds.
8:
Problem: we do not know why turnout in NEAR DAOs is low. We will interview 15 DAO members and publish a report with recommendations.
Budget: 3,000 USDC.
Researcher has a background in political science.

We will recruit 15 members across at least five NEAR DAOs using stratified purposive sampling by role and activity level. Interviews will follow a semi-structured protocol; findings will be coded thematically and validated through a public comment period. Deliverables: 10-page report, anonymized transcripts, prioritized action list, and a 20-minute community debrief. Budget: 1,200 USDC researcher time, 600 transcription, 400 participant incentives, 800 publication/outreach. Risks: low turnout; mitigation: pre-announced recruiting, reminders, and flexible scheduling.
